rulings.restated: Input — Did you pay for your shares, or for loans to the corporation, with money borrowed on terms that protect you from loss, such as a loan you are not personally liable for or one someone guarantees for you?
rulings.model: The question covers nonrecourse debt and guarantees but omits the third category: amounts 'covered by indebtedness from a person who has an interest in the activity or from a person related to a person (except you) having such an interest'. It also omits cash or property contributed to the activity that is itself so covered or protected.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the screen names nonrecourse and guaranteed borrowing but not the third source the instructions list, money 'covered by indebtedness from a person who has an interest in the activity or from a person related to a person (except you) having such an interest, other than a creditor' (i1120ssk p. 3, At-Risk Limitations), nor contributed cash or property so covered; a shareholder in that case answers No and the Form 6198 refusal does not fire (BUG-0914).

rulings.restated: Input — Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) take part in running it, for more than 500 hours a year, in at least 5 of the 10 years before 2025 (or any 3 earlier years, if it provides professional services)?
rulings.model: Tests 5 and 6 require that you 'materially participated in the activity for any 5 tax years' (or 3 for a personal service activity), which any of the seven tests can satisfy, not only 'more than 500 hours a year'. 'Professional services' also differs from the defined 'personal service activity', which includes any business 'in which capital isn't a material income-producing factor'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the question narrows an earlier year of material participation to 'more than 500 hours a year', but tests 5 and 6 count any year in which 'you materially participated in the activity' (i1120ssk p. 4, Individuals), by any of the seven tests, and a personal service activity is 'health, law, engineering, architecture, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, or consulting, or any other trade or business in which capital isn't a material income-producing factor', wider than 'professional services'. A shareholder who qualifies by another test answers No and box 1 is treated as passive (BUG-0913).

rulings.model: Box 2 income is always treated as passive, but the instructions say 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn't from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated'. No refusal names this case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; a real estate professional is refused by sche.re_pro (lane x1-sche, form sche: 'Schedule E, line 43 (real estate professional)'; scout-k1 R-K20), and in this tree scope.k1 still refuses every K-1 filer, so box 2 income or loss reaches no return as nonpassive. Integration must keep sche.re_pro asked of a K-1 box 2 filer.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "This Schedule K-1 passes every screen and its Form 7203 is supported" = true → helper "Passive income of boxes 1, 2 and 3"] [helper "This Schedule K-1 passes every screen and its Form 7203 is supported" = false → helper "Year parameter sales.zero"]
rulings.model: The restatement always treats box 2 income as passive and puts it in column (h). The IRS text says box 2 'isn't from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional (defined earlier) and you materially participated in the activity,' and in that case 'report box 2 income (loss) in column (i) or (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28'; no screen or refusal excludes real estate professionals.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; as in the first round of this line. A real estate professional who materially participated reports box 2 in column (i) or (k) (i1120ssk, box 2); the K-1 forms leave that case to sche.re_pro, which refuses a real estate professional (lane x1-sche, 'Schedule E, line 43 (real estate professional)'; scout-k1 R-K20), and in this tree scope.k1 still refuses every K-1 filer. The line was re-reviewed only because k1s.past_years (test 5/6) changed wording this round (BUG-0913); the reply raises nothing about that change.
